title: How Plumbers and Electricians Quietly Out-Earn Office Workers
description:
Plumbers and electricians earn more than the median American worker, start earning years earlier and often carry no student debt. Here are 12 quiet advantages of the trades, the honest downsides, and a lifetime money comparison.

Get The Ryan Rover Money Playbook: [LINK HERE]

Chapters:
0:00 Intro
1:56 How we got the numbers
2:31 Advantage 1. Pay above the median
4:10 Advantage 2. Paid to learn
5:30 Advantage 3. Little or no student debt
6:51 Advantage 4. A four year head start
8:07 Advantage 5. Overtime and emergency pay
9:31 Advantage 6. Side work
10:59 Advantage 7. A clear path to ownership
12:16 Advantage 8. Hard to outsource or automate
13:28 Advantage 9. A retirement wave creating demand
14:37 Advantage 10. Union benefits and pensions
15:43 Advantage 11. Lower cost of working
16:54 Advantage 12. Skills that save money at home
18:00 The honest downsides
19:06 Specialties where pay climbs higher
20:07 Three tradespeople, three paths
21:16 Money mistakes tradespeople make
22:30 A money plan for a new apprentice
24:10 Angle 1: The numbers
26:56 What office workers can learn from the trades
27:59 Angle 2: The psychology
29:44 Angle 3: The playbook
31:58 Questions people ask
33:25 Recap
34:27 What to do next

Sources:
- Bureau of Labor Statistics, Occupational Outlook Handbook: plumbers, pipefitters and steamfitters; electricians (median pay May 2023 about $61,550 and $61,590; job outlook)
- Bureau of Labor Statistics, Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics, May 2023 (median for all occupations about $48,060; top 10% of electricians above $100,000)
- Federal Reserve, Economic Well-Being of U.S. Households (student loans)
- Lifetime comparison: simplified illustration ($25,000 invested by age 22 at an illustrative 7% a year; $30,000 student loan)

Photos: Wikimedia Commons contributors. Full credits and licenses: https://github.com/ryan-rover-money-channel/ryan-rover-money/blob/main/agendamento/creditos/video20.md

This video is for education only and is not financial advice. Numbers are illustrations, not promises.
